assessment.nobel_worthiness: Defines incretin physiology (GLP-1 as a glucose-dependent insulinotropic and satiety signal) and led to a new drug class transforming treatment of type 2 diabetes and obesity, with documented cardiovascular and renal benefit. Combines fundamental physiology with very large, clear clinical impact.
assessment.attribution: Holst (physiology and secretion of GLP-1), Drucker (proglucagon biology and GLP-1 action) and Mojsov (identification of the active peptide form) are the strongest scientific core; Knudsen is an industrial developer of liraglutide and semaglutide, whose recognition is plausible but would crowd the three-person limit. Credit for the active GLP-1(7-36) form and the role of other contributors is contested to some degree.
assessment.maturity: Mechanism confirmed over decades by independent work, with large randomized outcome trials; the field is mature and the impact is now undeniable. Recognition is timely.
uncertainties: Allocation among Drucker, Holst, Mojsov, Knudsen and others (for example Habener) is not settled and I am relying on memory of the credit history.
Whether a prize would favour physiology or drug development is a matter of framing.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Optogenetics gave neuroscience and physiology a general method for causal, cell-type-specific control of activity with light, and is used across thousands of studies. The discovery of channelrhodopsins as light-gated channels plus their adaptation as neuronal tools is an original and lasting methodological advance.
assessment.attribution: Compound discovery: microbial rhodopsin biology (Bamberg, Nagel, Hegemann), the neuronal implementation (Boyden, Deisseroth) and earlier genetic photo-control (Miesenböck). The six credited names exceed three slots; the proposed trio pairs the channel discovery with the neuronal demonstration, but this is a judgement call that omits Boyden, Bamberg and Miesenböck.
assessment.maturity: Extensively reproduced and widely adopted for over fifteen years; clinical translation (vision restoration) is early but the tool's impact is established. Timely.
uncertainties: Fair allocation among six credited people is unresolved and I cannot verify the finer priority details.
A prize for a tool rather than a disease mechanism may be weighed differently by the full committee.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Genetically engineered T cells produced durable remissions in refractory B-cell malignancies and created a new therapeutic modality, with regulatory approvals and a growing set of applications including autoimmunity.
assessment.attribution: Rosenberg pioneered adoptive cell transfer and early gene-modified T cells, Sadelain developed the second-generation CD28 CAR concept and preclinical work, and June led the first clinical successes (4-1BB CAR, CLL). Others (Eshhar, Gross, Kuwana in early CAR concepts; Brenner, Rosenberg) complicate the picture, but the credited trio is a defensible configuration.
assessment.maturity: Clinical efficacy confirmed by multiple independent products and trials; long-term outcomes, toxicity and solid-tumour limits still evolving, but the core discovery is mature.
uncertainties: Early conceptual credit (chimeric receptor) outside the credited names may be material.
Long-term safety and generalisation beyond hematologic cancers remain uncertain.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Establishing long-lived self-organizing organoids from single adult Lgr5+ stem cells opened a platform for studying tissue renewal, disease modelling, host-pathogen work and personalised drug testing, built on the Lgr5 stem-cell discovery.
assessment.attribution: Clevers is clearly the intellectual leader (Wnt and Lgr5 intestinal stem cells and the organoid culture system); Sato was the lead experimentalist on the 2009 paper. A two-person allocation is clean from the supplied credit.
assessment.maturity: Widely reproduced across tissues and now used in clinical translational research; therapeutic impact is still emerging, so the case rests on the enabling-technology significance.
uncertainties: Relation to other organoid work (for example Sasai's) falls outside the supplied credit.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Massively parallel sequencing-by-synthesis transformed genomics, enabling population genomics, cancer genomics, rapid diagnosis and cell-atlas methods, with enormous downstream impact on biology and medicine.
assessment.attribution: Balasubramanian and Klenerman invented the reversible-terminator, single-molecule-array chemistry that became Solexa/Illumina; Mayer contributed to the parallel-cluster approach, but I am unsure of his relative weight. Wider contributions from other platforms (for example Church, Shendure, 454) are outside the supplied credit, which makes the allocation open.
assessment.maturity: Technology is entirely mature and universally used; recognition is overdue by impact but the field is crowded and a prize may raise whether it fits the category of a physiological discovery.
uncertainties: Whether platform and chemistry credit is cleanly assignable to two people.
Fit with the prize's discovery criterion is a judgement call.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Virus-like-particle HPV vaccines prevent persistent infection and are producing striking reductions in cervical precancer and cancer, a clear case of preventive medicine with global benefit.
assessment.attribution: Lowy and Schiller (L1 VLP self-assembly) and Frazer (with Zhou, the VLP/L1 and L2 work; the late Jian Zhou is not in the credited names) form the natural trio. Contribution of the late Zhou raises a posthumous-credit gap that I cannot resolve from the supplied credit.
assessment.maturity: Population-level effectiveness data, including strong evidence of cancer reduction in vaccinated cohorts, have matured; recognition is timely though the zur Hausen prize already honoured the viral cause.
uncertainties: Credit gap given Zhou's death and parallel work by other groups.
Overlap with the earlier HPV-cancer recognition may weigh against it.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Identification of cGAS as the cytosolic DNA sensor producing cGAMP, and of STING as its adaptor, established a central innate-immune pathway linking DNA sensing to interferon responses, autoimmunity, infection and cancer immunity.
assessment.attribution: Chen's identification of cGAS and cGAMP and Barber's discovery of STING are the two most decisive contributions; Ishikawa, Wu and Sun were key co-discoverers or trainees, and I would not add them within a three-person limit without more detail on their independent roles.
assessment.maturity: Highly replicated with many follow-up mechanisms; therapeutic translation (STING agonists, antagonists) is still in progress, so the maturity is strong for mechanism but modest for clinical effect.
uncertainties: Therapeutic proof is not yet established.
Credit for STING between Barber and others (for example Ishikawa, Tao Jin) is not fully resolved in the supplied text.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Antisense correction of SMN2 splicing (nusinersen) produced the first effective therapy for spinal muscular atrophy, transforming a fatal childhood disease and validating splice-modulating oligonucleotides as a modality.
assessment.attribution: Krainer (mechanistic splicing work and discovery of the ISS-N1 target in concert with collaborators) and Bennett (antisense chemistry and drug development) provide a compact two-person configuration. Contributions of others such as Hua and Singh in the splicing target may matter.
assessment.maturity: Approved with durable clinical benefit across multiple independent trials; broader platform impact for other splice-modulating drugs is still being shown.
uncertainties: Credit for identifying the intronic splicing silencer target may extend beyond the two credited names.
Clinical translation was an industry-academic collaboration, which may complicate how the discovery is framed.
